evals.prompt: I just published a new governance-kit release. Pull whatever's new into this repo.
evals.expected_output: Following UPDATE_FLOW.md Steps 1–8 under the repo-pinned model: the skill runs `kitverb.py kit-resolve` first — it reads the recorded pin (`kit_version: "0.1"`), resolves the target as the latest published `kit/vX.Y.Z` tag (provenance `published-tag`), fetches that tree into `~/.governance/cache/kits/`, and classifies `direction: forward`. The skill then runs the **fetched target's own** `kitverb.py kit-plan --diff` to resolve the managed-file inventory (`run.sh`, `lib.sh`, `enable-governance.sh`, `governance.yml`) with per-file diffs, shows the diffs (diff-before-exec), asks for explicit `yes`, and executes the apply as one `kitverb.py kit-apply` call against that same fetched engine — writing the stamped files, regenerating the hook dispatcher, rewriting `install.yaml.kit_version`, and smoke-testing. After the apply it records the pin via `kitverb.py kit-pin --kit-ref … --kit-sha …` (backfilling `kit_ref`/`kit_sha`, which this pre-#177 fixture lacks), then commits one atomic commit with subject `chore(governance): kit update 0.1 → <target>`. Pack updates are NOT chained because `--with-packs` was not requested.
assertions: The skill resolved the target via `kitverb.py kit-resolve` and the report's `Resolved:` row names the provenance (`published-tag`)
The recorded pin `kit_version: "0.1"` was read as the current version and `direction` was `forward`
The apply was delegated to the FETCHED target tree's own `kitverb.py` (kit-plan/kit-apply run from the cache dir), not the locally installed skill copy
The skill printed a per-file diff for each kit-runtime file BEFORE writing (diff-before-exec)
The skill asked for an explicit `yes` to execute (no silent acceptance)
`.governance/install.yaml` was rewritten with the new `kit_version`, and `kit_ref`/`kit_sha` were recorded via `kit-pin` (backfilled — the fixture had neither)
The hook dispatcher was regenerated (or explicitly noted unchanged)
Exactly one new commit was created with subject matching `chore(governance): kit update 0.1 → <target>` (with `(#N)` issue anchor)
Pack updates were NOT chained because `--with-packs` was not requested; the report says so
The skill did not push — the report's `Next:` reads `git push`

evals.prompt: Run governance kit update — I want to make sure we're synced.
evals.expected_output: Following UPDATE_FLOW.md Steps 1–2: `kit-resolve` resolves the latest published `kit/vX.Y.Z` tag and finds it equal to the repo's recorded pin (`kit_version: "0.4.0"`, `kit_ref`/`kit_sha` already present) → `direction: same`. The skill short-circuits the file apply, reports `kit: up-to-date`, and records the pin via `kit-pin` only if it changed (here it did not). No diffs, no file writes, no commit. The `Resolved:` row names the `published-tag` provenance — because the default target is now the published kit, "up-to-date" means current with the published release, not merely with the installed skill.
evals.expected_output_note: This fixture is already pinned (post-#177). If the latest published tag is newer than 0.4.0 the correct behavior is a forward update, not up-to-date; the assertions below grade the up-to-date branch as specified by the resolution provenance.
assertions: The skill resolved the target via `kit-resolve` and the `Resolved:` row names the `published-tag` provenance (not 'installed skill')
The skill reported `kit: up-to-date` (direction `same` — target equals the recorded pin)
No files were modified — runtime files, manifest, hook dispatchers, and lockfile are byte-identical to the fixture
No commit was created (the pin was already present and unchanged, so `kit-pin` was a no-op)
The skill did NOT walk the file inventory or print per-file diffs (the direction short-circuit precedes Step 3)
The report mentions that `--with-packs` was not requested (so pack-update chaining did not run)

evals.prompt: Update the kit in this repo.
evals.expected_output: Following UPDATE_FLOW.md Step 1's marker-reconstruction fallback: `kit-resolve`/`kit-plan` find `.governance/install.yaml` missing and reconstruct the pin by scanning kit-owned files for the `kit-version=<v>` marker token. The fixture's runtime stubs carry only the bare `# governance-kit:managed` marker (no `kit-version=`), so reconstruction yields nothing — the plan returns `delta: no-recoverable-pin` (`manifest_source: absent`). The skill refuses with the recovery path `governance uninstall` + `governance init` — without either the manifest or a versioned marker there is no recoverable pin.
assertions: No files were created, deleted, or modified
The plan returned `delta: no-recoverable-pin` after attempting marker reconstruction (scanning `kit-version=` in runtime files) — not an immediate refusal on missing manifest
The skill explained that reconstruction failed because the runtime files carry only the bare marker (no `kit-version=` token)
The skill named the recovery path: `governance uninstall` followed by `governance init`
The skill did NOT fall back to a heuristic that would invent a `kit_version`

evals.prompt: Pull the new kit version into this repo.
evals.expected_output: Following UPDATE_FLOW.md Step 2's downgrade rule under the repo-pinned model: `kit-resolve` reads `kit_version: "9.9"`, resolves the latest published `kit/vX.Y.Z` tag (some version below 9.9), and classifies `direction: downgrade`. Because `--allow-downgrade` was not passed, `kit-resolve` REFUSES and the refusal names the flag. The skill stops and tells the user that the repo is pinned to a kit newer than anything published, and that rolling backward needs the explicit `--allow-downgrade` flag. It does NOT silently downgrade.
assertions: No files were created, deleted, or modified
The skill refused because the resolved target is older than the repo's recorded `kit_version` ("9.9") — a downgrade
The refusal explicitly names the `--allow-downgrade` flag as the way to proceed
The skill did NOT auto-downgrade
The recovery path is to re-run with `--allow-downgrade` (not 'upgrade the kit on PATH' — version selection is now the manifest pin, not the installed skill)

evals.prompt: Sync the kit-runtime files in this repo to the latest version.
evals.expected_output: Following UPDATE_FLOW.md Step 2's pre-tracking-install case: `kit-resolve` resolves the published-tag target and the plan sees `kit_version` is absent from `install.yaml` → `delta: pre-tracking`. The skill offers to record the target version — consent is expressed by passing `--record-pre-tracking` to the delegated `kit-apply` (without it `kit-apply` refuses). It proceeds through the normal flow. Because the runtime stubs lack the line-2 ownership marker, every file surfaces as `Skipped (unmanaged)` in Step 4 and the user is asked per-file `keep` / `apply` / `overwrite-with-backup`; the choices go to `kit-apply` as `--decisions`. After the apply the manifest carries the new `kit_version` and the pin is recorded via `kit-pin`.
assertions: The skill detected that `kit_version` is absent from `install.yaml` and named it a pre-tracking install
The skill offered to record the resolved target version as part of the run (consent via `--record-pre-tracking`)
Each runtime file (`run.sh`, `lib.sh`) was surfaced as `Skipped (unmanaged)` because the line-2 marker is absent
For each unmanaged file, the skill asked per-file `keep` / `apply anyway` / `overwrite-with-backup` — no silent overwrite
If the user accepts any change, `.governance/install.yaml` was rewritten with the new `kit_version` and the `kit_ref`/`kit_sha` pin was recorded
Exactly one commit was created (or zero if the user declined every prompt and there was nothing to record)

evals.prompt: Update the kit in this repo.
evals.expected_output: Following UPDATE_FLOW.md Step 1's marker-reconstruction fallback: with `.governance/install.yaml` missing, the plan scans kit-owned files (`.governance/run.sh`, `.governance/lib.sh`) for the `kit-version=<v>` token, finds `kit-version=0.1` in both, and reconstructs the pin as `"0.1"` (the min) — `manifest_source: reconstructed`, `direction: forward`. The skill resolves the published-tag target, delegates `kit-plan`/`kit-apply` to the fetched engine (passing `--owner`/`--repo` so the fresh manifest can be written), shows per-file diffs, asks for `yes`, applies (re-stamping each marker, regenerating hooks, writing a fresh `install.yaml`), records the pin via `kit-pin`, and commits `chore(governance): kit update 0.1 → <target>`. The `Assumptions:` line records that the manifest was reconstructed from markers.
assertions: The plan attempted marker reconstruction before any user prompt and reported `manifest_source: reconstructed` with `installed_kit_version: 0.1`
`reconstructed_from` named at least `.governance/run.sh` and `.governance/lib.sh`
The apply was delegated to the fetched target tree's engine with `--owner`/`--repo` (the fresh manifest needs the repo identity)
Each rewritten runtime file was re-stamped with the new `kit-version=<target>` marker
A fresh `.governance/install.yaml` was written with the new `kit_version` and the `kit_ref`/`kit_sha` pin recorded
Exactly one new commit was created with subject `chore(governance): kit update 0.1 → <target>` (with `(#N)` issue anchor)
The `Assumptions:` line names the manifest reconstruction explicitly
The skill did NOT route to `governance uninstall` + `governance init` (that is the no-recoverable-pin case, eval 3)

evals.prompt: Pin this repo to governance-kit 0.4.0 exactly — not whatever the latest is.
evals.expected_output: Following UPDATE_FLOW.md with `--to 0.4.0`: `kit-resolve` resolves the exact `kit/v0.4.0` tag (provenance `explicit`), fetches it, and — since 0.4.0 ≥ the recorded `0.1` — classifies `direction: forward`. 0.4.0 is at the delegation floor (0.4.0), so it ships the engine. The skill delegates `kit-plan`/`kit-apply` to the fetched 0.4.0 tree, applies the stamped files, records `kit_ref: gh:…@kit/v0.4.0` + the resolved `kit_sha` via `kit-pin`, and commits. The `Resolved:` row reads `0.4.0 via explicit (--to)`.
assertions: The skill passed `--to 0.4.0` to `kit-resolve` and resolved exactly that version (provenance `explicit`), not the latest published tag
The fetched 0.4.0 tree's own engine performed the apply
`kit_ref` was recorded as `gh:duaility/governance-kit/governance@kit/v0.4.0` and `kit_sha` as the resolved 40-hex commit
The report's `Resolved:` row names the explicit (--to) provenance
One atomic commit was created; the skill did not push

evals.prompt: We need to roll this repo back to governance-kit 0.4.0 — it's currently on a newer kit. Use --allow-downgrade.
evals.expected_output: Following UPDATE_FLOW.md's downgrade path: `kit-resolve --to 0.4.0 --allow-downgrade` resolves 0.4.0, sees it is older than the recorded `9.9` → `direction: downgrade`, and (because the flag is set) proceeds. The downgrade is driven by the **newer local engine** applying the **fetched older** 0.4.0 assets + hook generator: `kit-resolve` names the local `engine_path` plus the fetched tree's `assets_root`/`hooks_lib`, and the skill runs `kit-plan`/`kit-apply` with `--assets-root … --stamp-version 0.4.0 --hooks-lib … --allow-downgrade`. Files are stamped `kit-version=0.4.0`, the manifest records `kit_version: "0.4.0"` and the 0.4.0 pin, and the report's `Assumptions:` notes the `--allow-downgrade` roll-back.
assertions: The skill passed `--allow-downgrade` and `kit-resolve` permitted the downgrade (it would refuse without the flag)
The apply ran the LOCAL engine against the FETCHED older tree's assets (`--assets-root`) and hook generator (`--hooks-lib`), stamping `--stamp-version 0.4.0` — the newer-engine / older-assets model
Runtime files were stamped `kit-version=0.4.0` and the manifest now records `kit_version: "0.4.0"` plus the 0.4.0 `kit_ref`/`kit_sha`
The report's `Assumptions:` names the `--allow-downgrade` roll-back
One atomic commit; no push

evals.prompt: I'm offline on a plane. Run governance kit update anyway.
evals.expected_output: Following UPDATE_FLOW.md's offline fallback: the skill passes `--offline` to `kit-resolve` (or `kit-resolve` degrades after a failed `git ls-remote`). With no network, resolution falls back through the repo's cached pin (`kit_ref`/`kit_sha` → a cached tree under `~/.governance/cache/kits/`) and then the installed skill, reporting which in the `Resolved:` row and an `Assumptions:` note. Since the cached pin equals the recorded `0.4.0`, this is `up-to-date`: no file writes, exit 0, never an error just because the network was unavailable.
assertions: The skill resolved offline without erroring — it did NOT fail the verb because the network was unavailable
The `Resolved:` row names the fallback provenance (`cache` if the pinned tree is cached, else `installed-skill`) and an `Assumptions:` note explains the offline fallback
Because the resolved target equals the recorded pin, the run was a clean `up-to-date` no-op (exit 0, no commit)
The skill pointed the user at refreshing the skill / re-running online to pick up a newer published release

evals.expected_output: Following UPDATE_FLOW.md's delegation floor: `kit-resolve --to 0.3.5` resolves 0.3.5, but 0.3.5 is below the delegation floor (`0.4.0`) — it ships no `kitverb.py` engine to delegate to. `kit-resolve` REFUSES (`floor_ok: false`), naming the floor and the legacy skill-reinstall path (`npx skills add Duaility/governance-kit#kit/v0.3.5 --global --skill governance --agent claude-code`, then run kit update from that skill). The skill surfaces the refusal and stops; nothing is fetched-and-applied.
assertions: The skill refused because the target 0.3.5 is below the delegation floor (0.4.0)
The refusal names the floor (0.4.0) and explains 0.3.5 ships no engine to delegate to
The recovery path names the legacy `npx skills add …#kit/v0.3.5` reinstall route
No files were created, deleted, or modified

evals.prompt: My installed governance skill is stuck on an old version, but I want this repo on the latest published kit. Run kit update.
evals.expected_output: Following UPDATE_FLOW.md's delegation contract (the version-skew case): even though the locally installed skill is on an older kit than the target, `kit-resolve` resolves the latest published `kit/vX.Y.Z` tag, fetches that tree, and the apply runs the **fetched target's own** `kitverb.py` — so the files written are exactly what the target version would write, byte-identical to running with a matching installed skill. The installed skill's version is no longer the ceiling; it is just the bootstrapper that resolves and delegates. The repo lands on the target version with its pin recorded.
assertions: The skill resolved the latest published tag as the target, NOT the (older) installed skill's version — the installed skill is not the ceiling
The apply was delegated to the FETCHED target tree's engine, so the result is byte-identical to a matching-skill run (markers stamped with the target version, written by the target's own code)
The repo's `kit_version` and `kit_ref`/`kit_sha` reflect the resolved target, not the installed skill
The skill did not require the user to refresh `npx skills` first to select the version — version selection happened through the manifest pin / resolution
